requirements.text: create an HR case for Aaron Le ... Open the case using the Password Reset service and include a short description noting his login access problem

cells.short_description: LIKE '%Service: Password Reset, Subject: Aaron Le, Detail:%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 13 AND opened_for = 91 AND status = 'ready' AND priority = 'moderate' AND short_description LIKE '%Service: Password Reset, Subject: Aaron Le, Detail:%' AND coe_type = 'HRIT' AND source IS NULL
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id is 60)
hr_service 13 is the active 'Password Reset' service
opened_for 91 is Aaron Le's HR profile (user 91); the column references hr_profile
status not stated; the policy's default for a new case is ready, and no assignment is asked for that would make it work_in_progress
priority not stated; the policy's default is moderate
short_description follows the policy template 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: .' naming the service and Aaron Le, as the benchmark tests; the wording of the detail is free
coe_type HRIT: the Password Reset topic sits in the 'Accounts / Account Access Control' category, whose coe_type is HRIT
source IS NULL kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (no channel is named)

requirements.text: attach an appropriate knowledge article as suggested, if available, that covers strong password creation and general account-security best practices
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_knowledge WHERE hr_case_kb_id = 13 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND knowledge_id = 5 AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_kb_id is 12); the task creates one link

knowledge 5 'IT Security Best Practices' is the only article on strong passwords and account security (the others cover benefits, onboarding, leave, travel and reviews); it is published, so linkable, and external, so visible to employees
used_as suggested, as the request says

requirements.text: Please create an HR case for Aaron Le
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'aaron.le@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'ready'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id is 60); the task creates one notification
the policy requires an update notification to the employee the new case is opened for, carrying the case's current status, which is ready
email aaron.le@servicenow.com kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy: it is Aaron Le's user email, the only address the listed tools return

notes:
The two independent readings agreed on every requirement, cell and value and on all three dispositions (all kept); their texts, assumptions and notes differ in wording only.
All 60 seed notifications go to the case subject's personal email (hr_profile.personal_email), whereas the benchmark expects Aaron Le's work email; no listed tool returns the personal email and the policy forbids assuming values, so the work email is kept.
Every case in the seed has a non-null source, while the benchmark expects none for this case; the request names no channel, so the benchmark's cell is kept.
opened_by is not tested: the policy calls it the requester, and the request does not settle whether that is the acting user, Robin Monroe, or the employee needing help; every seed case has opened_by equal to opened_for, and the benchmark does not test it.
The request asks the short description to note the login access problem; the wording is free (login, sign-in, access, password), so only the template's service and subject are tested, as the benchmark does.
The notification comes from the policy rule, not the request's words; the server may also send one automatically on registration, which the seed cannot show.
